observations: All eight physical clock-tail groups have 515 native cp-minus-cn Ic crossings in each of the three cases, matching the count of the actual parent and each of the four distributed base-access differences. The previous absence of collector-voltage-difference crossings therefore does not establish missing current steering. Count equality alone does not prove edge phase or sampler acceptance.

In nominal cases, C/D input-gain peak VCE remains 1.6708 to 1.6813 V while those same devices carry about 0.549 to 0.743 mA total Ic (Nx=4), below the per-emitter current limit. This is a headroom failure, not evidence of exceeding the saved current limit.
In hot_early, A/B hold devices 71/72/87/88 have active VCE minima 0.3585 to 0.3877 V at total Ic about 1.016 to 1.040 mA. At these exact rows B is above C; base/emitter currents were not saved.

Same-logical-net C/D follower-E to gain-B maximum voltage differences remain about 65.9 to 82.9 mV; follower-E to termination input-load differences are about 138.4 to 161.0 mV. These are distinct actual terminal routes at independently recorded extrema, not inferred resistor currents.

All 255 original fixed 0.3UI comparisons per sampler were searched with adjacent native rows kept. Nominal C/D worst margins remain negative; hot_early has negative worst margins on all four samplers.

next_correction_scope.reason: Actual native clock currents reverse in all eight branches; missing collector voltage zero crossings alone do not justify rewiring.
next_correction_scope.required_work: Use the published common native row ledger and exact source topology to design a bounded headroom/common-mode and remaining access-path correction. Preserve the separate gain and hold mechanisms and all original waveform/device gates; choose numerical component values only from a reviewable circuit derivation, then fresh physical/RC and native electrical proof.
